item.title: RPI football beats Ithaca, earns 1st berth in NCAA playoffs since 2021
item.description: RPI quarterback Justin McCormcak jumps through a hole during a game against Hobart on Sept. 26 in Troy. (Jim Franco/Times Union) Senior tight end Grayson Hunter caught two touchdown passes as the RPI football team edged host Ithaca 14-10 on Saturday to earn the program's first trip to the NCAA Division III playoffs since 2021. The Engineers (7-2 overall, 6-0 Liberty League) won their sixth straight game to secure at least a share of the title with Ithaca (7-2, 6-1). RPI gets the Liberty League's automatic bid to the NCAAs because of the head-to-head tiebreaker. "It's huge," RPI coach Ralph Isernia said. "It's something we've been working for, especially with this senior group the last four years. The time in the weight room and the time on the practice field, time in film meetings, all that stuff." RPI, which snapped a four-game losing streak against Ithaca, can win the league outright by beating Union College for the Dutchman Shoes Trophy in Troy next Saturday. Hunter, a backup behind starter Josh Young, made a diving 15-yard touchdown catch from starting quarterback Micah Balzarini for a 7-7 tie with 1:16 left in the second quarter. With 4:22 left in the third quarter, Hunter caught a 19-yard pass from backup quarterback Justin McCormack on a ball that was tipped by an Ithaca defender to put RPI ahead 14-10. "Certainly, there's a lot of attention that goes to Josh Young, and that's understandable," Isernia said. "But (Hunter) is able to get open and he's made plays for us this entire year." Isernia said McCormack came into the game for Balzarini by design. "Obviously, he brings another dimension with the run game and he's also an extremely effective passer as well," Isernia said. RPI's defense held Ithaca well below its league-leading average of 40.3 points per game. Defensive linemen Owen Boland and Cameron Keeperman combined on a sack of quarterback Michael Reed that helped stop a late Bombers drive. On the game's final play, Ithaca threw a Hail Mary pass from the RPI 48 that fell incomplete in a crowd in the end zone. RPI's Aidan Bekkenhuis was credited with the breakup. item.title: Messi's Miami cling to second spot on dramatic final MLS day
item.description: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami are guaranteed homefield advantage in at least their opening two rounds of post-season (Megan Briggs) Lionel Messi's Inter Miami clung on for second place in the Eastern Conference with a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the MLS regular season Saturday. The Argentine superstar set up the first two goals at Miami's Nu Stadium, both from corners, to procure the reigning champions home-field advantage in at least their opening two rounds of the playoffs. Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada's brace soon after the break sparked a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko's late strike in a game characterized by awful defending at both ends. A single point proved enough. Miami finished the regular season second on 60, as third-place New England Revolution failed to take advantage with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando, finishing on 58. Messi's men will now face the Columbus Crew to begin the playoffs. Runaway leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. Though he did not get on the scoresheet himself Saturday, Messi's 26 goals this season are still almost certain to seal his second straight golden boot award. Petar Musa, whose FC Dallas were in action later Saturday, would need to score five to prevent Messi becoming the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boots. Charlotte had an early goal ruled out in the Miami clash for handball against Idan Toklomati, who set up Abada after intercepting Casemiro's weak defensive header back to the goalkeeper. In the 14th minute, Messi's corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte's Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring for Miami. Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suarez wide open at the near post. The Uruguayan glanced in his header for 2-0, with Messi picking up the assist. De Paul made it three before halftime, given time and space by Charlotte's defense to slam a long-range shot low to the goalkeeper's right and into the side netting. Early in the second half Abada pulled back a goal for the visitors, blasting home substitute Tyger Smalls' sharp cut-back pass from Ashley Westwood's incisive aerial through ball. Minutes later, Messi uncharacteristically steered wide a straightforward header from the edge of the six-yard box. Abada bagged a second in the 55th minute, stunning a crowd that had been in party mood moments earlier, with a first-time finish after a one-two with Pep Biel who played a smart backheel return pass. In the 90th minute, Aloko bagged the equalizer, responding first to the ball as Smalls' shot ricocheted off the post. A visibly frustrated Messi hit the post in stoppage time before Aloko came inches from bagging an unlikely winner with a thunderous shot into the outside netting. item.title: Analysis: Turnovers, missed tackles and lack of discipline cost No. 9 BYU a chance to upset No. 3 Utah
item.description: BYU Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) falls short of a touchdown during the first half of a football game against the Utah Utes, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City. | Erin Hooley, Deseret News A lot of numbers were thrown around before No. 9 BYU traveled to No. 3 Utah in the most significant football rivalry game in the long, heated and often tumultuous series between the Beehive State foes. When it was over in front of 52,901 at Rice-Eccles Stadium, only one digit really stood out. That would be four. The upset-minded Cougars blew a rare opportunity to get a win in Salt Lake City, get their College Football Playoff hopes back on track and snap their rivals’ nation-best winning streak on Saturday afternoon. The number everybody on the blue side will remember is the four turnovers BYU committed against a ballhawking Utah defense that was otherwise pushed around most of the day. So the undefeated Utes ran off with a 28-20 victory — snapping the Cougars’ three-game winning streak against them — and put what was once the most-anticipated season in school history on life support. Although BYU head coach Kalani Sitake wouldn’t dare say it himself — preferring to heap praise upon the Utes than say the Cougars simply committed far too many turnovers and mental mistakes to win — the truth is that BYU faltered in the second half, while Utah soared. The Utes had the clutch gene in beating the Cougars for the first time since 2019, and BYU did not. The Cougars got away with an awful second half in their 28-24 win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame that now seems like a distant memory, but that kind of failure never works in this rivalry. Neither team is ever out of the games in this wild and wacky rivalry. Leave it to BYU freshman Legend Glasker to sum up what happened to the Cougars (4-2, 7-2), who must now win out and hope that either Houston or Texas Tech loses down the stretch. “I feel like the second half we got too big-headed and thought the game was ours and it just slipped away,” he said. item.title: Former UH coach Dana Holgorsen fired as Nebraska offensive coordinator following Huskers loss
item.description: Nebraska offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen looks on before the game between the Washington Huskies and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 31, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, Nebraska. (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) A little more than three years after boasting "There ain't no f- hot seat in my mind," Dana Holgorsen has been fired for a second time. Nebraska fired its offensive coordinator, who was the head coach at the University of Houston when he had his hot seat discussion, Saturday, a day after the Cornhuskers lost to Illinois 24-13, their fourth straight loss after they opened the season 5-0. Nebraska scored just 54 points combined in those four losses, failing to score more than 17 in any of the defeats. "Like so many of you, I am angry, I am disappointed and I am frustrated with our results this season," Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said in a statement released Saturday. "As the head coach, I am ultimately responsible for every aspect of our program - including wins and losses - and it is my responsibility to make changes when they are warranted. "While there are many areas that need improvement, our offensive plan and execution is simply not working. Earlier today, I relieved offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen of his duties. As I have recently shared, Dana has a fantastic offensive mind, he is a strong leader, and he has done great work here at Nebraska. But simply, we need a change." A year after being fired by UH following a disappointing 2023 season, Holgorsen was hired at Nebraska as an offensive consultant late in the 2024 season . He moved into the offensive coordinator's role before last season, getting a contract that paid him $1.2 million annually. Holgorsen's offense ranked 12th (22.2 points per game) in the Big Ten in scoring in conference games. The Huskers ranked eighth (25.4) last season. The 55-year-old Holgorsen once was thought of as an offensive coaching savant with his stints as coordinator at Texas Tech, UH and Oklahoma State earning him his first head coaching job at West Virginia. Holgorsen led the Mountaineers to three Top 20 finishes in eight seasons, including an Orange Bowl win in his debut season in 2012. He resigned his post at West Virginia in 2019 to return to Houston as head coach. The Cougars went 31-28 in five seasons with Holgorsen at the helm, including a 12-2 run in 2021 when UH finished the season ranked 17th in the country. The Cougars dipped to 8-5 the next season, which is when the hot seat talk started. "We won bowl games in back-to-back years," Holgorsen told The Athletic in March 2023 . "I have five years on my contract with a f- impossible buyout. … So there ain't no f- hot seat in my mind. There just ain't." Eight months later, the Cougars finished off a 4-8 season and Holgorsen was given a $14.8 million buyout. Holgorsen had a brief stint as a consultant at TCU before joining Rhule in Nebraska. item.title: Utah’s Big Win Proves Dampier Is Heisman-Ready
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Utah put an end to the three-game losing streak in the Holy War with a 28-20 win over BYU on Saturday. The third-ranked Utes stayed unbeaten and kept their College Football Playoff hopes alive. Devon Dampier accounted for four total touchdowns to lead the way. It was a statement game for the program, but the coach wants the team to keep grinding. Dampier Makes His Case Devon Dampier is the Big 12’s clearest Heisman candidate after Saturday’s performance. He has now thrown for a touchdown in eight of nine games this season while adding a pair of rushing scores against BYU. The senior signal-caller threw two scores and ran for two more against the Cougars. He also caught a 29-yard pass between two defenders to keep a drive alive. The Big 12 has not had a national finalist since TCU in 2022. A Heisman winner has not come from the conference since Oklahoma left. If the league is going to break that streak, it has to be Dampier. Defense Forces The Turnovers The Utes defense picked off BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier four times on Saturday. Bachmeier threw for 272 yards and a touchdown, but he could not protect the ball. Through the initial eight games of the season, he totaled four picks, plus two additional ones in the fourth quarter versus Utah. Both of those late interceptions happened inside the end zone. Utah forced three turnovers in the second half and shut out the Cougars for the rest of the game. The defense held BYU to just 39 yards in the third quarter. That stop allowed Utah to take the lead for good. Utah started the game with a burst of speed that put them ahead 14-0 in less than five minutes. It took just 75 seconds for the Utes to drive 75 yards for the first score. Utah’s opening drive leading to a touchdown marked the eighth occurrence this season. The team has now outscored opponents 103-9 in the opening quarter through nine games. Head coach Morgan Scalley knows the team is in the driver’s seat for a title, but he does not want them to get comfortable. Following the game, Scalley said on the broadcast, “This was a big win, not THE big win,” according to Fox Sports . The Utes remain 9-0 and 6-0 in the Big 12.

item.title: Former Missouri QB Chase Daniel calls out ‘ridiculous’ fumble ruling in Texas win
item.description: Arch Manning’s throwing arm was already coming forward when Brian Huff of the Missouri Tigers hit him on third-and-10 late in the third quarter Saturday. The ball traveled 14 yards past the line of scrimmage, the officials in Columbia, Missouri, ruled it a fumble, and replay let the call stand. Instead of facing fourth-and-10, the Texas Longhorns had a first down and a drive that tied the game three plays later. Texas trailed 20-13 at the Missouri 39 with 2:22 left in the quarter. Most players stopped once the ball hit the turf, and Texas receiver Emmett Mosley V scooped it up for what officials credited as a fumble recovery past the line to gain. Referee David Smith announced after the review that the ruling on the field stood, and the Faurot Field crowd booed. Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) reacts during the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at the Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The NCAA rule book says a forward pass begins with any intentional forward movement of the passer’s hand while the ball is firmly in his control, unless he clearly starts bringing it back to his body. Replay could only confirm a fumble by deciding Manning had lost firm control before that forward motion began, and the slow-motion angles appeared to show the ball still in his hand as his arm moved. Overturning a call requires indisputable video, and the booth decided those angles did not meet that standard. Did one ruling decide Texas’ win at Missouri? Manning found a wide-open Jermaine Bishop Jr. for a 25-yard touchdown on the next third down to tie it at 20, and Texas never trailed again. The Longhorns scored 21 straight points, with Raleek Brown catching the go-ahead touchdown from Manning with 5:03 left and running for the clincher with 1:25 to go. Manning finished with 297 yards and three touchdown passes in the 34-20 win. Former Missouri quarterback Chase Daniel weighed in on X before the game was over, pointing to the reaction inside ESPN’s booth, where Jesse Palmer worked the game alongside Joe Tessitore. “This is the most ridiculous call I’ve ever seen….you have the rules analyst and Jesse Palmer on the broadcast completely flabbergasted,” Daniel wrote . item.title: Did Jack Campbell’s Injury Influence the NFL’s Decision Not to Fine Him?
item.description: The NFL announced its Week 8 fines on Saturday, and two Detroit Lions players found themselves opening their wallets. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams were each fined $11,941 for taunting during Detroit’s 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings. But there was another play from that game that caught my attention. One involving Jack Campbell . And considering what happened to Campbell later in the game, I can’t help but wonder whether the NFL’s decision not to fine him was influenced by the circumstances. Let me be clear. I’m not suggesting the NFL intentionally covered anything up. There is no evidence of that. But after reviewing the earlier tackle, I believe it’s a fair question to ask. Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (46) looks on during Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jack Campbell’s Earlier Tackle Raises Questions Most Lions fans remember the frightening scene during the fourth quarter when Campbell suffered a serious neck injury while tackling former Detroit tight end T.J. Hockenson. Campbell was eventually taken to a hospital, and the organization has understandably made his health and recovery its top priority. However, there was another tackle earlier in the game that deserves attention. With 2:33 remaining in the third quarter , Campbell appeared to lower his head and initiate contact with the crown of his helmet while making a tackle. Dr. Jimmy Liao, who analyzes Detroit Lions injuries, reviewed the footage and identified the earlier collision as potentially significant. item.title: Hutchinson beats Buatsi to win WBC light-heavyweight title
item.description: Willy Hutchinson (left) became only the second man to defeat Joshua Buatsi as a professional [Queensberry Promotions] Willy Hutchinson was crowned the WBC light-heavyweight champion after he produced the performance of his career to beat Joshua Buatsi in Manchester. Hutchinson, 28, edged the tense rematch with the judges scoring it 117-112, 115-113, 115-113 to avenge his defeat by Buatsi in 2024. Saturday's contest was initially for the interim title but was upgraded when American David Benavidez gave up the WBC gold to move up to cruiserweight. Scotland's Hutchinson and Londoner Buatsi met for the second time, just over two years after the Londoner earned a split-decision win in a thrilling first contest, but this time it was Hutchinson who came out on top as he improved his record to 21 wins with two defeats. It was a childhood dream come true for Hutchinson, who said before the fight he wrote about his dreams of becoming a WBC champion at the age of 13. An emotional Hutchinson said after his win was confirmed: "I want to tell the story one more time. I was 13-years-old. My dad was working in Sweden. I signed it in a book, I said I will become a world champion. Let's go! "Can I say thank you to my coach because I'll you one thing, without him I don't think I'll be here today let alone boxing. This man dug me out of a hole that I never thought that I would get out of, so this is all a bonus baby." Buatsi looked a shadow of the fighter who put Hutchinson on the canvas twice in their first meeting, seeming short of ideas on how to catch the slick Scot. Ticket sales were modest for a world title fight as it was clear that it did not capture the attention of the British public. But those inside made the atmosphere as raucous as possible, with the Manchester crowd favouring Hutchinson. And they were delighted when the result was read out and Hutchinson became the eighth British light-heavyweight champion - the first since Nathan Cleverly in 2017. Hutchinson shows class to join British elite Fight week was dominated by predictions that Buatsi, five years Hutchinson's senior, is over the hill. And the Londoner did nothing to prove otherwise as Hutchinson often toyed with his opponent in the centre of the ring. The first fight in 2024 had Buatsi walking to the ring as a comfortable favourite, and he backed that up with crushing body shots to send Hutchinson tumbling twice. But this time around, Hutchinson was a different fighter. In his own words, he had "matured" after picking up two wins since last facing Buatsi. Hutchinson clearly had the crowd on his side as he made the walk to cheers, while Buatsi was met by a chorus of boos as he paraded around the ring before the bell. For Buatsi, the strategy was very much the same as the first encounter - whip shots into the body - but Hutchinson now had answers.
